headline: Machine learning models span antimicrobial, toxicity, PROTAC, and siRNA design tasks
label: Ai Driven Molecular Property Prediction
summary: Preprints now pair graph, hypergraph, and generative models with ADMET, toxicity, and phenotypic endpoints for compound prioritisation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning applied to molecular prioritisation, spanning graph-based QSAR, hypergraph and ensemble networks, and diffusion or GAN-based generation. Several items address antimicrobials: an XGBoost and GNN screen of Zinc20 for membrane-active compounds reports that training-set bias limits hits against novel targets, and a hypergraph model classifies antimicrobial combinations as synergistic, antagonistic, or non-interacting. Toxicity and ADMET prediction appear in a graph-transformer model linking Caspase-3/7 activation and mitochondrial membrane potential loss to DILI labels, and in ADMETron's 34-endpoint platform benchmarked on TDC. Design-oriented work includes PhenoCompass, which co-embeds structures with Cell Painting morphology for virtual phenotypic screening, FENNEC for chemically modified siRNA efficacy, and DesignMaster for linker-conditioned PROTAC generation. The published Fung-AI study reports GAN-generated antifungal peptides with mild activity against Fusarium graminearum.
